problem: Existing spatial-intelligence benchmarks test isolated relations, directions or targets, and navigation benchmarks entangle waypoint choice with mapping, memory and control. None directly measures whether a VLM can pick a geometrically feasible, goal-consistent, embodiment-aware waypoint route from a single first-person view.
motivation: Zero-shot navigation systems increasingly rely on VLMs to choose spatial actions from the current observation. This requires target recognition, action-consequence assessment, distance estimation and path planning to work jointly. A verifiable, scene-grounded evaluation of this joint decision is needed, along with training data to improve it.
key_idea: Overlay numbered waypoints on rendered egocentric RGB views registered to 3D scenes, and score a VLM's returned waypoint set or ordered route against point-agent and embodied (0.6 m body) geometric feasibility graphs and goal regions.
insight: VLMs judge local actions reasonably (traversability BA up to 77.9%) and pick a legal first edge (88-96%), but fail to keep routes legal across later edges (illegal later edges in 42-76% of routes even with a correct first edge and goal) and to ground the terminal waypoint. This persists on sparse overlays and short references, so route length or clutter does not explain it. Removing the image or mismatching the overlay drops SR to about 0, so the tasks need the paired visual input. SFT on the released geometry-grounded data raises the score from 3.9 to 38.9 and transfers to external spatial benchmarks.
method: Waypoint interface: numbered visible ground waypoints plus non-traversable surface/object negatives are projected into the egocentric RGB image, each anchored to a 3D scene location; the model returns a JSON list of IDs
Five tasks: Point Traversability, Embodied Traversability (set output); Point Path, Embodied Path (explicit target), Intent Path (intent plus visual cue; ordered route)

Geometry-grounded construction: scenes from InternScenes (3RScan, ScanNet, ARKitScenes, Matterport3D); point and embodied (0.6 m diameter) free-space graphs; reference routes searched separately and projected into the view; unverifiable routes discarded

Question and Spatial CoT generation: language produced after target, waypoints and routes are fixed; Intent descriptions must resolve uniquely in the view; GPT-5.5 writes Spatial CoT for the training split only

Route evaluator: ordered checks for parse, valid IDs, required start, legal consecutive edges, and acceptable endpoint. Metrics are BA/F1, VPR, SR, SPL, and an EgoPath Score that equally averages chance-adjusted BA (2BA-1) for the two traversability tasks and SR for the three route tasks
Challenge-set selection: bundle-level selection of hard cases (clutter, boundaries, point-vs-embodied differences), with splits by source scan group (31,852 train / 1,345 val / 1,111 benchmark)
Training resource study: LoRA SFT of Qwen3.5-4B (rank 8, vision tower frozen, two stages) on the images, Spatial CoT and JSON answers

setting.backbone: Nine zero-shot VLMs (Gemini 3.1 Pro, GPT-5.5, Claude Opus 4.8, MiniMax M3, Qwen 3.6, Mistral L3, Llama 4, Kimi K2.6, Grok 4.3), all frozen; Qwen3.5-4B fine-tuned with LoRA in the training study
setting.model_size: Qwen3.5-4B for the fine-tuned model; proprietary models unspecified; Llama 4 Maverick 17B-128E; Mistral Large 3 675B
setting.training_data: EgoPathBench train split: 31,852 questions with GPT-5.5 Spatial CoT and geometry-verified answers (zero-shot VLMs use no training)
setting.observation: single egocentric RGB image with numbered waypoint overlay, plus text prompt
setting.action_space: selection of numbered visible waypoint IDs (set or ordered route)
setting.simulator: Blender 4.4 rendering of static indoor scenes (InternScenes); no interactive simulator
setting.privileged: none at inference for the model; the evaluator uses registered 3D scene geometry and reference routes

numbers.extra: trained on the 31,852-question EgoPathBench train split with GPT-written Spatial CoT

numbers.eval_set_note: 1,111 benchmark questions; best zero-shot model (benchmark evaluation only)

numbers_note: This is a benchmark paper with no standard VLN benchmark results. The 'test' split label is used for the paper's own benchmark split. Zero-shot results for the other eight VLMs appear in Table 1 and are not repeated here.
results: The best zero-shot VLM (Gemini 3.1 Pro) scores 28.3, ahead of GPT-5.5 at 27.3 and Claude Opus 4.8 at 25.6. It reaches 35.9% SR on Point Path but only 2.9% on Embodied Path and 4.0% on Intent Path. On a 50-question subset a human scores 54.2 versus 28.6 for the best VLM. SFT of Qwen3.5-4B lifts the score from 3.9 to 38.9 and improves all four external evaluations by 1.4-9.6 points.
limitations: Single static RGB view with a predefined waypoint overlay; it does not test closed-loop navigation, mapping, memory or replanning, and the waypoint vocabulary is given rather than generated
The benchmark is a hard-selected subset built from a small set of rendered indoor scan assets; the human reference is only 50 questions from one volunteer; each model was evaluated in a single pass
Fine-tuned in-domain gains may reflect the same generator, task format and GPT-written CoT; external transfer gains are modest (1.4 on 3DSRBench)
